title: A Release That Reaches the Robot: Target, Manifest, Version, Fit, Install and Trial in One Pipeline, Cut at Every Step

questions.question: Why is 1.10.0 newer than 1.9.0, and what goes wrong with a text comparison?
options: It is not newer: 1.9.0 is the larger
As text and as numbers the answer is the same
1.10.0 is newer only if the patch is larger
By number 10 is more than 9, while as text 1.10.0 sorts before 1.9.0
questions.explanation: Versions are compared number by number. Compared as text, the character 1 comes before 9 and the newer release looks older.

questions.question: A rollback to 1.2.0 is authorised on a robot with a floor of 1.3.0. What does decide say?
options: install: the rollback was authorised
refuse below the minimum: the floor cannot be authorised away
refuse older
refuse invalid
questions.explanation: A rollback can be authorised down to the floor and no further. Below the floor is a release with a fault that must never run again.

questions.question: Eight bad releases were offered. What was true of the disk after each refusal?
options: Nothing was written: the pointer was where it was and slot 1 was still empty
The new release was half written to slot 1
The boot pointer had moved to slot 1
The old release had been erased
questions.explanation: Target, manifest, version and fit are all checked before anything is written. A refusal leaves the robot exactly as it was.

questions.question: Power is lost after each of the ten steps of the install. How many robots were bricked, and how many ended on the new release when it was run again?
options: 10 bricked and none recovered
5 and 5
0 and 10 of 10
None bricked, and none on the new release
questions.explanation: Every cut left the robot booting 1.4.2, and running the same install again finished on 1.5.0 each time.

questions.question: A release is healthy for 90 s and then crashes at every boot, with a soak of 30 s. What did the pipeline report?
options: Rolled back to 1.4.2 after four boots
Confirmed, running 1.5.0, and not up
Refused at the trial stage
Bricked, with nothing booting
questions.explanation: It was confirmed at 50 s, before it crashed, so the trial could not catch it. Healthy at 20 s plus a soak of 30 s confirms at 50 s. The crash at 90 s then belongs to a confirmed release, with nothing to fall back to.

questions.question: A release crashing on 300 of 1000 robots is rolled out in waves. What happened?
options: All 1000 were given it and 300 rolled back
It was refused at the manifest
The rollout halted at wave 0 after 10 robots
300 were bricked before it halted
questions.explanation: 9 on the new release, 1 rolled back, none bricked. The robot with the fault failed its trial and rolled back, and the rollout counted that failure and stopped. The two mechanisms did their separate jobs.
